headline: A 2005 executive order handed off certain presidential duties for appointing new military officers and chief warrant officers to other officials.
what_it_does: This order assigns, or delegates, certain functions related to first-time appointments of commissioned officers and chief warrant officers in the U.S. armed forces. In practice, an order like this usually lets officials such as the Secretary of Defense handle some appointment steps that the law gives to the President. Only the title was provided, so the exact duties and who receives them are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: People receiving first-time appointments as commissioned officers or chief warrant officers
who_it_affects.how: Their appointments may be handled by officials the President named rather than by the President directly.
They may gain responsibility for certain officer and warrant officer appointment duties.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed July 27, 2005; exact effective date not stated in the material provided.
